status: Proposed; no internal module has an assessed teaching score

modules.title: What our people are doing with AI
modules.owner: Cyber AI adoption lead + champions from all six functions
modules.why: N1 needs credible examples from colleagues, evidence of results and a clear distinction between available tools and emerging capabilities.
modules.agenda: 10m orientation; 35m two colleague-led case demonstrations including a failure and its correction; 15m an emerging or restricted-pilot demonstration; 15m domain application; 15m knowledge check and reflection. Use a short case gallery to represent all six functions without six separate lectures.
modules.evidence: N1.1: explain one own-domain and one neighbouring-domain use case, including limitations. N1.2: distinguish production, restricted pilot and horizon examples. N1.3: propose two or three changes to own work and identify retained human accountability.
modules.prerequisites: Case owners provide verified examples, permission to demonstrate them, evidence of results and current tool-access status.

modules.title: Our approved tools, agent architecture and boundaries
modules.owner: AI platform owner + IAM + IDP + security architecture
modules.why: Only internal owners can establish the approved platforms, data routes, identities, access limits and escalation mechanisms.
modules.agenda: 25m model, modality and agent walkthrough; 25m approved platforms, data flow and connector permissions; 20m approval, logs and stop controls; 20m access/data-boundary decisions. Use one real approved architecture with a simplified diagram.
modules.evidence: Label model, harness, tools and controls; select the permitted platform for a data class; distinguish available access from a pilot; locate the correct approval, stop and escalation route.
modules.prerequisites: Current platform inventory, data-handling rules, approved access routes, accessible demonstration and reviewed diagrams.

modules.title: Safe use in my job — coached case and Gate 1
modules.why: A local exercise tests judgement against the bank rules after the external foundation, without repeating general AI-awareness content.
modules.agenda: 15m coached case; 30m individual safe-use scenario; 15m feedback. Use approved or synthetic data and a task representative of the learner’s function.
modules.evidence: Reject an unsafe data/tool choice, detect a planted unsupported claim or injection, verify the output and record accountability. Safety-critical decisions must pass.
modules.prerequisites: Independent answer key, domain case variants, accessible format and calibrated assessor checklist.

modules.title: Supervise and recover an agent on our platform
modules.owner: Domain operations owner + AI platform team
modules.why: Supervision depends on the actual console, action permissions, logs, approvals and recovery runbook.
modules.agenda: 30m workflow and permissions; 60m trace-review and planted-error lab; 30m stop, revoke, rollback and manual-fallback exercise.
modules.evidence: Delegate within an approved action class, inspect permissions and changes, identify planted failures, stop/revoke safely and produce an accountable handover.
modules.prerequisites: Stable approved sandbox or realistic simulation, seeded traces and a tested recovery path.

modules.title: Create, own and retire a shared Skill
modules.owner: Domain automation champion + Skill-library owner + IAM
modules.why: The catalogue has no evidenced teaching for Skill maintenance and shared-library ownership; internal conventions must be taught directly.
modules.agenda: 30m worked example and third-party vetting; 60m create a focused Skill and safe connector specification; 30m peer review, ownership, monthly review and deprecation.
modules.evidence: Submit a trigger, steps, expected output, failure modes and tests; name an owner and review/deprecation rule; justify connector permissions and provenance.
modules.prerequisites: Agreed Skill template, library workflow, ownership rules, approved connector list and model-change notification route.

modules.title: Domain test cases and release checks
modules.why: Useful benchmark answers and known faults come from the function’s own work; a generic course cannot supply the approved cases.
modules.agenda: 30m independent answers and known faults; 60m build and run five representative cases with pass/fail checks; 30m simulate a model/Skill change and submit results to the domain evaluation process.
modules.evidence: Versioned cases, known faults and acceptance checks; rerun record; contribution to the shared domain evidence store.
modules.prerequisites: Labelled cases, approved data, a simple supported evaluation harness and result-submission format.

modules.title: Agent-supervisor observed sign-off
modules.why: Course completion cannot establish safe operational supervision in this environment.
modules.agenda: 75m observed task with injected faults and a connector change; 30m independent challenge; 15m feedback and scope-of-authority record.
modules.evidence: Pass each safety-critical action and justify an evidence-based release decision. Record permitted action classes and any remediation.
modules.prerequisites: Assessor calibration and test cases withheld from coached practice.

modules.title: Workflow and supervision design studio
modules.owner: Process owner + technical lead + operational supervisor
modules.why: N14 concerns real workflow allocation, approval gates, workload and accountability. A workshop with the actual process owner is more actionable than generic organisational-redesign teaching.
modules.agenda: 45m map current work; 60m redesign tasks and approval points; 45m review evaluation evidence and supervision load; 30m agree measures and ownership.
modules.evidence: An approved before/after workflow, human/agent task split, supervision ratio hypothesis, autonomy limits supported by evaluation, value baseline, owner and refresh plan.
modules.prerequisites: One candidate workflow, operational baseline and access to the process owner.

modules.title: Build, evaluate and secure a scoped agent
modules.owner: AI engineering + AppSec + domain evaluation lead
modules.why: The capstone must exercise approved architecture, identities, deployment controls and bank-specific test evidence.
modules.agenda: 2h configure an existing approved scaffold; 2h tests and human-label calibration; 2h attack, recovery and production-monitoring rehearsal; 1h evidence dossier. Reuse one project across the pathway.
modules.evidence: Versioned implementation and test cases, human-checked judge results, working controls, attack/recovery trace, monitoring and ownership record.
modules.prerequisites: Prepared scaffold and sandbox; Python readiness. Seven hours assumes adaptation of a scaffold, not a production build from scratch.

modules.title: Independent technical challenge
modules.why: An independent test establishes the demonstrated scope and residual gaps.
modules.agenda: 75m reproduce an unseen failure and recovery; 30m design/evidence challenge; 15m feedback and permitted-scope record.
modules.evidence: Reproducible test evidence and pass on all critical controls within the authorised action class.
modules.prerequisites: Calibrated challenge pack distinct from practice.

modules.title: Workflow, supervision and accountability studio
modules.why: N14 concerns real workflow allocation, approval gates, workload and accountability. A workshop with the actual process owner is more actionable than generic organisational-redesign teaching.
modules.agenda: 30m current workflow; 45m autonomy/approval design; 30m value and oversight measures; 15m ownership agreement.
modules.evidence: An approved before/after workflow, human/agent task split, supervision ratio hypothesis, autonomy limits supported by evaluation, value baseline, owner and refresh plan.
modules.prerequisites: Use the same workflow and shared studio template as technical colleagues.

modules.title: Bank AI-risk and assurance evidence case
modules.owner: AI risk lead + assurance lead + domain evaluator
modules.why: Risk acceptance, vendor approval and control ownership depend on the internal governance process.
modules.agenda: 1h inventory and risk scenario; 1h control/vendor dossier; 1h independent-test and judge-evidence review; 1h risk decision and escalation. Map local obligations only for the role and jurisdictions concerned.
modules.evidence: Traceable risk decision, control evidence, vendor challenge, human-labelled evaluation sample and named residual-risk owner.
modules.prerequisites: Approved templates, risk appetite, review forum and a redacted vendor/use-case dossier.

modules.title: Independent governance challenge
modules.why: Assess whether the learner can challenge evidence and defend a decision.
modules.agenda: 75m evidence challenge; 30m reviewer calibration; 15m feedback and decision-rights record.
modules.evidence: Defend the risk decision with test evidence, recognise weak automated evaluation and specify unresolved conditions.

modules.title: Operating-model and tool-selection decision studio
modules.owner: CIO strategy lead + process owners + AI risk lead
modules.why: N14 concerns real workflow allocation, approval gates, workload and accountability. A workshop with the actual process owner is more actionable than generic organisational-redesign teaching.
modules.agenda: 30m workflow/value baseline; 45m vendor and autonomy decision; 30m supervision capacity and junior-skill retention; 15m ownership and next evidence request.
modules.evidence: An approved before/after workflow, human/agent task split, supervision ratio hypothesis, autonomy limits supported by evaluation, value baseline, owner and refresh plan. Challenge at least one vendor claim and one weak evaluation result.
modules.prerequisites: Common studio template, vendor evidence and budget/role constraints.

modules.title: Quarterly evidence and adoption forums
modules.why: Leaders need repeated decisions using actual adoption and control evidence.
modules.agenda: Four 1h forums: baseline and test-set quality; autonomy and judge validation; production drift/value; refresh and accountability. Include a short coached lesson before the decision.
modules.evidence: Four decision records connecting evaluation results to adoption, supervision capacity, permissions and investment.
modules.prerequisites: Quarterly portfolio evidence, human-labelled samples and attendance by accountable owners.

buildEstimateBasis: Initial planning allowances in person-hours for a reusable pilot pack, including SME design, instructional design, review and pilot repair; not vendor quotes. Exclude learner time, delivery, translations, travel, platform engineering and ongoing updates. Shared N14 template design counted once in IH-08T; governance/leadership rows are adaptations.
casesAre: Candidate briefs, not claims about existing deployments

cases.evidence: Show source traceability, a missed/incorrect signal, analyst correction and measured review effort.
Show data boundaries, a misclassification and the human decision.
Show authoritative source links, an unsupported claim and reviewer correction.

cases.candidate: Code finding explanation and test generation
cases.evidence: Show a false positive, reproducible test and developer review.
Show identity/permission limits, an escalation and retained human approval.

cases.candidate: Tool comparison and adoption decision support
cases.evidence: Show test evidence, cost/oversight assumptions and a rejected vendor claim.
